source.author: lucr
source.text: Denique caelesti sumus omnes semine oriundi; omnibus ille idem pater est, unde alma liquentis umoris guttas mater cum terra recepit, feta parit nitidas fruges arbustaque laeta et genus humanum, parit omnia saecla ferarum, pabula cum praebet, quibus omnes corpora pascunt et dulcem ducunt vitam prolemque propagant; qua propter merito maternum nomen adepta est.
source.text_original: Denique caelesti sumus omnes semine oriundi; / omnibus ille idem pater est, unde alma liquentis / umoris guttas mater cum terra recepit, / feta parit nitidas fruges arbustaque laeta / et genus humanum, parit omnia saecla ferarum, / pabula cum praebet, quibus omnes corpora pascunt / et dulcem ducunt vitam prolemque propagant; / qua propter merito maternum nomen adepta est.
source.text_english: Finally, we are all sprung from heavenly seed; that same father is for all, from whom the fostering mother earth received the drops of liquid moisture, and, made fruitful, bears shining crops and cheerful trees and the human race, and bears all the generations of wild beasts, while she provides their food, by which all creatures feed their bodies and lead a sweet life and propagate offspring; wherefore she has rightly gained the name of mother.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: itaque non errat Lucretius, cum dicit: denique caelesti sumus omnes semine oriundi, omnibus ille idem pater est .
reuse.text_original: itaque non errat Lucretius, cum dicit: denique caelesti sumus omnes semine oriundi, omnibus ille idem pater est .
reuse.text_english: And so Lucretius is not wrong when he says: in the end, we are all born from heavenly seed; he is the same father of all.
